title: Brown butter and hazelnut gateau
subtitle: a rich, nutty gateau with a brown butter financier-style sponge and praline buttercream
excerpt: Brown butter and hazelnut gateau is a layered cake with a hazelnut financier-style sponge, made with browned butter and ground hazelnuts in place of most of the flour. The sponge has a deep, nutty flavour and a dense, moist crumb. It is filled and coated with a hazelnut praline buttercream and finished with caramelised hazelnut shards.
sourceNotes: Financier-style sponge cakes, made with browned butter (beurre noisette) and nut flours, are a classic of French patisserie. The term financier refers specifically to the small rectangular cakes named for the Paris financial district. Adapting this sponge into a layered gateau is a contemporary home-baking approach influenced by French patisserie techniques.

glossaryTerms.definition: Unsalted butter cooked in a pan until the milk solids toast to a golden-brown and the butter takes on a nutty, caramel-like smell. Also called beurre noisette.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sponges can be made the day before and stored wrapped at room temperature. The hazelnut praline keeps in an airtight container for up to a week. Assemble on the day.

content.text: Brown butter and hazelnut gateau is a layered cake built on a sponge that uses

and ground hazelnuts in place of most of the flour. The result is a dense, moist crumb with a deeply nutty flavour. The brown butter is made first and left to cool, so it goes into the batter as a liquid. The hazelnut praline for the buttercream is made with caramelised sugar and hazelnuts, then ground to a coarse paste.

Make the brown butter: melt the butter in a light-coloured saucepan over medium heat. Continue cooking, swirling occasionally, until the butter smells nutty and the milk solids at the bottom have turned deep golden-brown. Pour immediately into a bowl and leave to cool to room temperature.

Make the praline: heat the caster sugar in a dry pan until amber. Add the hazelnuts, swirl to coat, and pour onto baking paper. Once cold and hard, blitz to a coarse crumb in a food processor. Reserve some whole pieces for decoration.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease and line two 20 cm round cake tins.

Whisk the eggs and caster sugar together until pale and thick, about 4 minutes with an electric mixer. Mix in the vanilla. Fold in the ground hazelnuts, flour, and baking powder. Drizzle in the cooled brown butter and fold to combine.
Divide between the prepared tins. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 15 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.

Make the praline buttercream: beat the softened butter until pale. Add the icing sugar in two additions and beat until smooth. Mix in the crushed hazelnut praline and cream. Beat for 2 minutes. Layer and coat the cakes with the buttercream. Scatter praline pieces on top.

attrs.problem: Brown butter going too dark and tasting burnt rather than nutty
attrs.avoid: Avoid high heat or leaving the pan unattended; the colour change from golden to burnt happens very fast.
attrs.fix: Use a light-coloured pan so you can see the colour change clearly. Once the solids are deep golden-brown, pour immediately into a cool bowl to stop the cooking.

attrs.problem: Sponge very dense and flat rather than light
attrs.avoid: Avoid deflating the egg and sugar foam when adding the flour and butter.
attrs.fix: Fold the flour in gently with a large metal spoon, working from the bottom of the bowl upward. Add the brown butter in a thin drizzle around the edge of the bowl rather than pouring it directly onto the batter.
